text:
jess: Quick heads-up — after today's kernel rollout I'm seeing p99 spikes on long-context (8k) workloads. Tail looks like a queue-delay hump, not pure kernel slowness. :thinking:
matt: Can you paste the profiler link and the config for the scheduler?
jess: profile: https://perf.internal/fg/2143219876 (flame + queue heatmap). Scheduler snippet: ```
max_batch_tokens=4096
max_wait_ms=8
kernel_routing=auto
kv_prefetch=true
```
tina: Interesting. The heatmap shows a cluster of requests sitting ~12-18ms in the queue before dispatch. That matches a microbatching threshold boundary.
rico: Is the KV cache warm for those traces? If kv_prefetch=true but hit rate is low we pay extra prefetch + dispatch handoff cost.
jess: KV hit rate for the trace is ~72% overall, but p99 requests have <40% kv hit. Looks like tail requests miss the cache and trigger prefetch which delays dispatch.
anya: That could explain why p95 is fine but p99 jumps — tail misses cause longer scheduling + kernel cold path.
matt: Two levers to try: 1) reduce max_wait_ms to force earlier dispatch (reduce tail queue delay), 2) bump max_batch_tokens so more inputs can batch quickly and amortize KV miss overhead. Both have throughput/latency tradeoffs.
jess: Proposed experiment: A/B for 2h: group A (baseline) max_wait_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=4096; group B max_wait_ms=4, max_batch_tokens=8192. Measure p95/p99, tokens/sec, KV hit by quantile.
perf-bot: /run-experiment name=kv-prefetch-handoff-2143219876 groups=2 duration=2h
deploy-bot: Canary started on 5% of traffic for group B.
anya: Also add a kernel_routing override: prefer "fallback-eager" for requests with seq_len>6000 so kernel handoff happens earlier instead of trying auto decision. That reduces recompile/handshake latency.
jess: Good point. I'll enable forced routing for the canary. Updated config for group B: ```
max_batch_tokens=8192
max_wait_ms=4
kernel_routing=fallback-eager
kv_prefetch=true
```
rico: Watch out for throughput drop if max_wait_ms too low — you can lose batching efficiency and increase per-token cost. We'll track cost metrics.
matt: If group B lowers p99 without throughput loss, we can consider making it a global default for long-context models.
jess: Early 30-min snapshot: group B p99 down from 320ms -> 210ms, p95 steady, tokens/sec -3%. KV hit unchanged overall but tail miss rate reduced slightly (40%->34%). Good signal.
anya: That suggests routing change helped handoff latency. Next step: try disabling kv_prefetch in group C to see if prefetch itself is causing the dispatch stall (i.e., post-dispatch prefetch vs pre-dispatch).
jess: I'll schedule group C tomorrow: max_wait_ms=4, max_batch_tokens=8192, kernel_routing=fallback-eager, kv_prefetch=false.
perf-bot: Reminder: add the eval prompt set for long-context regression checks (p99 generation correctness) before any global rollout.
matt: SGTM. Add a config flag to trace per-request events: [queue_enter, kv_fetch_start, kv_fetch_end, dispatch_start] so we can quantify handoff latency.
jess: Added traces. Thanks everyone. Action items: run group C, collect 2h metrics, share flame + event timelines, then decide global flip. :rocket:
